rule:
For every proposition (propositions.jsonl) and every branch (branches-D5.jsonl):
  - the kind declared (`carried_by` for a proposition; a branch's `shared_warrant`, `form_or_grouping`, `confidence`);
  - the evidence named: a proposition's `rests_on` (arrows and elements), `finding`, `evidence_gate`; a branch's
    `binds`, `construct_bindings`, `verdicts`, the propositions it holds and fails;
  - the `rival` (a proposition's), or that none is named;
  - the validation it received, by kind, from the records the claim names:
      pattern: each arrow it rests on with its counts (holds, both, share or the like), whether a denominator is
        given, whether the arrow beat its base rate (`base_rate_beaten`), and its bracket fields (`before_h73`,
        `early_late`), against prior.md section 4's brackets;
      words: the exemplar concepts the arrows and findings cite (resolved against codes.jsonl), and the return's
        verdicts on the elements (adaptations by op, from adjudications.jsonl accepted lines).
A claim validated with the other kind's evidence is judged by hand in the audit section; the script lays the fields
side by side and resolves every concept it cites. prior.md section 3's declaration and literature-C3.md's switch
records are read by hand there too.

propositions.level: element: a chain of three arrows, each with its own mechanism
propositions.rival: The order is how threads are made: a call is a thread's title and the build reports are comments under it, so the order follows the coders' choice of turns.
propositions.evidence_gate: rooms carrying both elements of each arrow; the order statement 'in a room carrying both, the first concept of FROM comes before the first concept of TO', against 500 shuffles within each room (seed 20261014)
propositions.falsify_elsewhere: On another shared surface with a per-account rate limit, groups would build before anyone calls as often as after, or keep a finished work no more often than an unfinished one.
propositions.statement: When a member starts a mark (R01), the room calls others to place (P01); after a call, the room builds the mark and members report it (P03); once the mark stands, the room keeps it (P05).

propositions.level: dimension: Maintenance to Order without law; the three arrows share the mechanism that keeping a work brings a room into relations with other rooms; A19 is thin
propositions.rival: Neighbours were there from the room's first post, so the talk comes with the spot and not from keeping it.
propositions.evidence_gate: rooms carrying both elements of each arrow; the order statement 'in a room carrying both, the first concept of FROM comes before the first concept of TO', against 500 shuffles within each room (seed 20261014)
propositions.falsify_elsewhere: On another shared surface, groups that keep their work would meet their neighbours no more often after upkeep than before it.
propositions.statement: When a room keeps a mark (P05), it turns to other rooms: it talks borders with neighbours (P08), asks other rooms for help (P16) and joins coalitions under attack (P17). Where border talk comes before upkeep, it mostly offers terms before any damage.

propositions.level: element: a chain; A16 and A17 share the mechanism that a contest is answered by the order between rooms (Contention to Order without law); A15 and A18 have their own
propositions.rival: Restraint is coded only when there is an attack call to refuse, so the order is built into the coding (A16 is partly constitutive).
propositions.evidence_gate: rooms carrying both elements of each arrow; the order statement 'in a room carrying both, the first concept of FROM comes before the first concept of TO', against 500 shuffles within each room (seed 20261014)
propositions.falsify_elsewhere: In another population, attack calls would draw no refusal inside the calling group, or refusals would come as bare as acceptances.
propositions.statement: A call to place can turn members against a rival's work (P01 to P09). The same room answers the call to attack: members refuse it, in written replies usually with a reason (F-014), the room reins in the attackers or apologises (P07), or points to a truce (P08). Where the attack goes on, the rooms ca…

propositions.level: dimension: Coordination without command to Imprinting (A07), then inside Imprinting (A08, A09)
propositions.rival: Celebrations and records cluster at the end of the event in every room, so the order is the clock's and not the room's.
propositions.evidence_gate: rooms carrying both elements of each arrow; the order statement 'in a room carrying both, the first concept of FROM comes before the first concept of TO', against 500 shuffles within each room (seed 20261014)
propositions.falsify_elsewhere: In another episode with an imposed end, groups would record before they celebrate as often as after.
propositions.statement: After members report a mark done (P03), the room celebrates it (P11), records what it celebrated (P12) and carries the record on (P13). Placement stops at hour 73 for every room; after it, rooms can celebrate, record, curate the record and carry it on, and no one can place.

propositions.level: dimension: Critical mass to Host framing
propositions.rival: A removal needs a post to remove, so the line follows a call by definition (A20 is partly constitutive).
propositions.evidence_gate: rooms carrying both elements of each arrow; the order statement 'in a room carrying both, the first concept of FROM comes before the first concept of TO', against 500 shuffles within each room (seed 20261014)
propositions.falsify_elsewhere: In another passing event inside standing communities, the communities would contain it as often before any member posts about it as after.
propositions.statement: When a room calls for hands in a standing sub (P01), the host sub's moderators and members draw a line around canvas talk (P20): a megathread, removals by rule, a canvas sub, objections to the flood.

propositions.level: dimension: Maintenance to Coordination without command
propositions.rival: The members who run scripts are the members who keep the work, so the order follows who is active, not strain.
propositions.evidence_gate: rooms carrying both elements of each arrow; the order statement 'in a room carrying both, the first concept of FROM comes before the first concept of TO', against 500 shuffles within each room (seed 20261014)
propositions.falsify_elsewhere: Under a per-account rate limit elsewhere, groups would turn to automation before any upkeep as often as after.
propositions.statement: When the room's upkeep needs more placements than its members can make (P05), members turn to scripts and spare accounts (P14).

propositions.level: element: two theorised arrows and claims on findings (F-021, F-023, F-006)
propositions.rival: Members decided their organization in chats that the record does not hold, so the absence of decided order is the instrument's.
propositions.evidence_gate: rooms carrying both elements of each arrow; the order statement 'in a room carrying both, the first concept of FROM comes before the first concept of TO', against 500 shuffles within each room (seed 20261014)
propositions.falsify_elsewhere: In another population whose chats are on the record, decisions about who does what would appear wherever the work was large.
propositions.statement: Rooms align their members' placing without deciding how they are organized: members answer a call in a bare line (P15), a design argued in a thread is settled by a posted template (P04), and a decided element of order appears in 46 of 705 rooms (C01). propositions.level: dimension: Critical mass to Order without law; one thin arrow
propositions.rival: Rooms move by a coalition's plan or by choice, and the judgment of too few hands is written after the move.
propositions.evidence_gate: rooms carrying both elements of each arrow; the order statement 'in a room carrying both, the first concept of FROM comes before the first concept of TO', against 500 shuffles within each room (seed 20261014)

propositions.statement: When a room judges it has too few hands to hold its spot (K02), it stops fighting for it and moves (P10), and members keep calling for the new spot.

propositions.rival: Sparing is tacit and comes first, and help comes with the neighbour, not with the border.

propositions.statement: A settled border (P08) opens a channel through which the two rooms trade help (P16).
